744:     @staticmethod
745:     def _status_for(readiness: ConsolidationReadiness) -> RunStatus:
746:         # A run cannot be COMPLETED while required stages are missing; the
747:         # only question is whether we reached a validated, mapped position.
748:         if readiness.missing_required_stages:
749:             has_errors = any(
750:                 i.severity is Severity.ERROR for i in readiness.issues
751:             )
752:             return RunStatus.FAILED if has_errors else RunStatus.BLOCKED
753:         return RunStatus.COMPLETED
754: 
755:     @staticmethod
756:     def _summary(readiness: ConsolidationReadiness) -> str:
757:         completed = ", ".join(readiness.completed_stages) or "none"
758:         if readiness.complete:
759:             return (
760:                 f"FY{readiness.period} group consolidation completed: "
761:                 f"{len(readiness.completed_stages)} stage(s) completed "
762:                 f"({completed}); consolidated statements and deliverables "
763:                 f"written to /output."
764:             )
765:         blocked = ", ".join(readiness.blocked_stages) or "none"
766:         return (
767:             f"FY{readiness.period} consolidation readiness: "
768:             f"{len(readiness.completed_stages)} stage(s) completed "
769:             f"({completed}); {len(readiness.blocked_stages)} blocked "
770:             f"({blocked}). Consolidation is NOT complete: required stages "
771:             f"missing ({', '.join(readiness.missing_required_stages)})."
772:         )
773: 
774:     @staticmethod
775:     def _answer(readiness: ConsolidationReadiness) -> str:
776:         lines = [
777:             f"Consolidation readiness for FY{readiness.period} "
778:             f"(scope: {readiness.scope}).",
779:             "",
780:             "Stages:",
781:         ]
782:         for stage in readiness.stages:
783:             mark = {
784:                 "completed": "x",
785:                 "blocked": " ",
786:                 "pending": " ",
787:                 "failed": "!",
788:             }[stage.status.value]
789:             lines.append(f"  [{mark}] {stage.stage} — {stage.status.value}"
790:                          f"{' (' + stage.detail + ')' if stage.detail else ''}")
791:         lines.append("")
792:         for name in readiness.entities:
793:             r = readiness.entity_results.get(name)
794:             if r is None:
795:                 lines.append(f"{name}: not processed")
796:                 continue
797:             lines.append(
798:                 f"{name}: {r.row_count} rows, balanced={r.balanced}, "
799:                 f"mapped={r.mapped_row_count}, unmapped={r.unmapped_row_count}"
800:             )
801:         lines.append("")
802:         if readiness.complete:
803:             lines.append(
804:                 "The group consolidation completed end to end. The consolidated "
805:                 "statements and the seven deliverables were written to /output."
806:             )
807:         else:
808:             lines.append(
809:                 "The consolidation is NOT complete: at least one required stage "
810:                 "did not finish. No consolidated statements should be relied on."
811:             )
812:         return "\n".join(lines)
813: 
814:     def _reject(
815:         self, field: str, message: str, details: dict[str, Any]
816:     ) -> SkillResult:
817:         return SkillResult(
818:             status=RunStatus.FAILED,
819:             summary=f"invalid consolidation request: {message}",
820:             answer=message,
821:             data={"validation_error": True, "field": field, **details},
822:             issues=[
823:                 {
824:                     "code": f"invalid_{field}",
825:                     "severity": Severity.ERROR.value,
826:                     "message": message,
827:                 }
828:             ],
829:         )
830: 
831:     def _error_result(self, exc: LedgerFlowError, period: str) -> SkillResult:
832:         return SkillResult(
833:             status=RunStatus.FAILED,
834:             summary=f"consolidation blocked by {exc.code}: {exc.message}",
835:             answer=exc.message,
836:             data={"period": period, "error_code": exc.code},
837:             issues=[
838:                 {
839:                     "code": exc.code,
840:                     "severity": Severity.ERROR.value,
841:                     "message": exc.message,
842:                 }
843:             ],
844:         )

1: """Consolidation run persistence (filesystem, no database).
2: 
3: Each run is stored as one JSON file under ``storage/runs/<run_id>.json`` using
4: the existing atomic-write primitive, so a run survives a backend restart and
5: can be re-fetched by id. This is the minimum needed to support the
6: ``GET /api/consolidations/runs/{run_id}`` refresh path — no new persistence
7: system is introduced, and no PostgreSQL is required.
8: """
9: 
10: from __future__ import annotations
11: 
12: from datetime import datetime, timezone
13: from pathlib import Path
14: from typing import Any
15: 
16: from app.core.errors import NotFoundError, StorageError
17: from app.storage.filesystem import atomic_write_json, read_json
18: 
19: 
20: class ConsolidationRunStore:
21:     """Read/write consolidation run records on the filesystem."""
22: 
23:     def __init__(self, runs_dir: str | Path) -> None:
24:         self.runs_dir = Path(runs_dir)
25: 
26:     def _path(self, run_id: str) -> Path:
27:         if not run_id or "/" in run_id or "\\" in run_id or ".." in run_id:
28:             raise StorageError("invalid run id", details={"run_id": run_id})
29:         return self.runs_dir / f"{run_id}.json"
30: 
31:     def exists(self, run_id: str) -> bool:
32:         return self._path(run_id).is_file()
33: 
34:     def save(self, record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
35:         """Persist a run record (``created_at`` set once, preserved on rewrite)."""
36:         run_id = str(record.get("run_id") or "")
37:         path = self._path(run_id)
38:         now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
39:         created_at = now
40:         if path.is_file():
41:             try:
42:                 created_at = read_json(path).get("created_at", now)
43:             except StorageError:
44:                 pass
45:         stored = {**record, "created_at": created_at, "updated_at": now}
46:         atomic_write_json(path, stored)
47:         return stored
48: 
49:     def list(self, limit: int = 50) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
50:         """Return stored runs, newest first (by ``created_at``).
51: 
52:         Corrupt/unreadable records are skipped rather than failing the whole
53:         listing, so one bad file cannot hide the run history.
54:         """
55:         if not self.runs_dir.is_dir():
56:             return []
57:         runs: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
58:         for path in self.runs_dir.glob("*.json"):
59:             try:
60:                 data = read_json(path)
61:             except StorageError:
62:                 continue
63:             if isinstance(data, dict) and data.get("run_id"):
64:                 runs.append(data)
65:         runs.sort(key=lambda r: r.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)
66:         return runs[:limit]
67: 
68:     def load(self, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
69:         """Return a stored run, or raise ``NotFoundError``."""
70:         path = self._path(run_id)
71:         if not path.is_file():
72:             raise NotFoundError(
73:                 "consolidation run not found", details={"run_id": run_id}
74:             )
75:         data = read_json(path)
76:         if not isinstance(data, dict):
77:             raise StorageError(
78:                 "corrupt consolidation run record", details={"run_id": run_id}
79:             )
80:         return data

# LedgerFlow Consolidation Workflow: Backend → Frontend Map

## 0. Wiring overview

`backend/app/main.py:79-81` sets the three seams the router reads off `app.state`:

```python
application.state.runner_factory = runner_factory or _default_runner_factory
application.state.run_store = ConsolidationRunStore(storage_paths.runs_dir)
application.state.traces_dir = storage_paths.traces_dir
```

`_default_runner_factory` (`main.py:34-39`) builds a fresh `AgentRunner(default_runtime(build_default_registry()))` per run — production uses the loopback MCP gateway. Router mounted at `main.py:93`.

## 1. `backend/app/api/consolidations.py` — every endpoint

Prefix `/api/consolidations` (line 51). Five endpoints.

### 1a. `POST /runs` → `start_run` (lines 175-209)
- **Request:** `ConsolidationRunRequest` (`schemas/consolidation.py:16-38`): `period` (default `"FY2024"`), `scope` (default `"group"`), optional `entities: list[str]`. `model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}` (line 25) — unknown fields rejected.
- **Invocation** (lines 186-196):
```python
payload = {"period": body.period, "scope": body.scope}
if body.entities:
    payload["entities"] = body.entities
result = await runner.run(mode=AgentMode.CONSOLIDATION, payload=payload)
record = _result_payload(result.run_id, result, created_at="")
stored = store.save(record)
response = _to_response(stored)
```
- **Execution is synchronous** — the HTTP response is the completed `AgentRunner` result (module docstring lines 10-14).
- **Status codes** (lines 199-209): `400` if `skill_data.get("validation_error")` or error code `intent_identification_failed`; `500` if `result.status.value == "failed"`; else `200`. The structured run body is preserved even on 400/500.
- **Response:** `ConsolidationRunResponse`.

### 1b. `GET /runs` → `list_runs` (lines 236-270)
- Query `limit: int = 50`. Returns `ConsolidationRunListResponse` with compact `ConsolidationRunSummary` rows (newest first via `store.list`). Pulls `period` from `readiness`, and headline figures from `consolidated_summary` falling back to `control_figures` (lines 255-267).

### 1c. `GET /runs/{run_id}` → `get_run` (lines 273-288)
- Loads saved record via `store.load`; **404 JSON** body `{code, message, details}` on `NotFoundError`. Returns full `ConsolidationRunResponse`.

### 1d. `GET /runs/{run_id}/trace` → `get_run_trace` (lines 291-329)
- Loads record, then reads JSONL trace events via `TraceRecorder(traces_dir, record["trace_id"])` (lines 309-322). Returns `ConsolidationTraceResponse` = `{run_id, trace_id, events[], tool_calls[]}`.

### 1e. `GET /output/{filename}` → `download_output` (lines 212-233)
- Serves a deliverable file from `settings.output_dir`. Path-traversal guarded (lines 219-229): rejects `/`, `\`, `..`. Media type `application/json` for `.json`, else `text/csv`.

### How the run record is built/saved — `_result_payload` (lines 114-147)
Stored record fields (this is exactly what `ConsolidationRunStore.save` persists):

```python
{
  "run_id", "trace_id", "mode", "status", "summary", "skill_name", "created_at",
  "readiness": readiness.model_dump() if readiness else None,
  "skill_data": _jsonable(skill_data),
  "consolidated_summary": (skill_data or {}).get("consolidated_summary"),
  "control_figures": _jsonable((skill_data or {}).get("control_figures")),
  "statements": (skill_data or {}).get("statements"),
  "output_files": list((skill_data or {}).get("output_files", [])),
  "issues": [i.model_dump() for i in _issues(result)],
  "tool_calls": [t.model_dump() for t in result.tool_calls],
  "errors": [e.model_dump() for e in result.errors],
  "warnings": list(result.warnings),
  "ai_configured": ..., "ai_stages": ..., "ai_reasoning": ...,
}
```
Note the record **contains the full statements, control figures, consolidated summary and output manifest** — but see §5 for what the frontend does with them.

`_readiness` (lines 70-92) extracts `ReadinessModel` from `skill_result.data` (guarded by `"stages" in data`). `_issues` (95-98) maps `skill_result.issues`.

### `ConsolidationRunStore` (`backend/app/services/consolidation_runs.py`)
- Filesystem JSON at `storage/runs/<run_id>.json`. `save` (34-47) sets `created_at` once and always overwrites `updated_at`; `list` (49-66) sorts by `created_at` desc, skipping corrupt files; `load` (68-80) raises `NotFoundError`.

## 2. Agent execution — `graph.py`, `runner.py`, `state.py`, `thread_service.py`

### `state.py`
- `AgentMode` (20-24): `CONSOLIDATION`, `COPILOT`.
- `RunStatus` (27-35): `running`, `completed`, `completed_with_warnings`, `blocked`, `failed`, `awaiting_review`.
- `SkillResult` (72-81): `status`, `summary`, `answer`, `data`, `issues`, `tool_calls`.
- `AgentState` (83-102, TypedDict): `mode, run_id, thread_id, trace_id, user_input, payload, history, messages, intent, skill_name, skill_result, tool_calls, errors, warnings, status, summary`. Reducers: `add_messages`, `operator.add` for tool_calls/errors/warnings.
- `ExecutionResult` (105-119): final API-facing result — `run_id, trace_id, thread_id, mode, status, summary, intent, skill_name, skill_result, tool_calls, errors, warnings`.

### `graph.py`
Flow: `START → load_context → identify_intent → select_skill → execute_skill → finalize → END` (lines 454-475).
- **Consolidation intent is deterministic, no LLM** — `consolidation_intent` (166-181) builds `Intent(kind="consolidation", confidence=1.0, source="deterministic")`. `identify_intent` (237-308) path at 242-248.
- `execute_skill` (353-421): resolves skill from registry, binds the MCP gateway to the skill's static `ToolPolicy`, builds `SkillContext`, calls `await skill.execute(context)`, de-dupes tool records from the gateway (412-416), sets `skill_result`, `tool_calls`, `status`.
- `finalize` (423-452): status/summary from `result`; only successful runs produce an `AIMessage` (438-440).
- `default_runtime` (492-515): real `SkillRegistry`, LLM provider `create_chat_model(app_settings)`, `ThreadService(storage_paths.threads_dir)`, `traces_dir`, loopback `ToolGateway(MCPClient(settings.mcp_server_url))`.

### `runner.py`
- `AgentRunner.run` (69-182): mints `run_id`/`trace_id` (93-94); copilot (not consolidation) gets a thread; loads history; builds `initial: AgentState` (115-128); invokes graph with `recursion_limit = max(10, agent_max_graph_steps)` (52-53); on crash returns `ExecutionResult(status=FAILED)` (135-174); persists thread only when one exists (178-180); returns `_to_result` (189-210).
- **Consolidation runs are stateless** (no thread persisted) — see comment lines 102-104.

### `thread_service.py`
Filesystem JSON per thread at `storage/agent_logs/threads/<thread_id>.json`. `serialize_message`/`deserialize_message` (36-57); `save` preserves `created_at` (98-127); `load` returns `[]` if absent; `delete` (140-146). **Not involved in consolidation runs** — only copilot threads.

### What the final result payload contains
`ExecutionResult.skill_result` is the whole consolidation payload (see §4). The API then flattens it into the stored record in `_result_payload` (§1).

## 4. What the consolidation skill actually produces

`backend/app/agents/skills/consolidation.py` — despite the docstring (lines 13-24) saying translation/elimination/statements are "blocked", the **actual implemented code performs full assembly** (lines 302-341):

```python
assembly_ok = False
...
from app.accounting.outputs import OutputWriter
from app.accounting.statements import StatementAssembler
assembler = StatementAssembler(self._source)
bundle = assembler.assemble(selected)
writer = OutputWriter(self._settings.output_dir)
output_manifest = writer.write_all(bundle)
assembly_ok = True
...
control_figures = bundle.control_figures
statement_payload = bundle.statements.model_dump()
consolidated_summary = self._financial_summary(control_figures)
```

It attaches to `SkillResult.data` (lines 390-403):
```python
data["statements"] = statement_payload          # balance_sheet / profit_and_loss / changes_in_equity / checks
data["control_figures"] = control_figures       # 12 figures
data["consolidated_summary"] = consolidated_summary  # 4 headline figures + currency
data["output_files"] = output_manifest          # 7 deliverables
data["ai_stages"] = [...]; data["ai_reasoning"] = {...}; data["ai_configured"] = ...
```

`_finalize` status (`_status_for`, 744-753): `FAILED` if errors, `BLOCKED` if required stages missing, else `COMPLETED`. `STAGE_ORDER` in `consolidation.py:51-65` now marks **all 12 stages implemented=True**.

`StatementAssembler` (`accounting/statements.py`) builds real consolidated BS/P&L/changes-in-equity and `control_figures` (893-906). `OutputWriter.write_all` (`accounting/outputs.py:73-85`) writes **7 files**: `consolidated_tb.csv`, `balance_sheet.json`, `profit_and_loss.json`, `changes_in_equity.json`, `eliminations.csv`, `issues.json`, `control_figures_ns.json`. These appear in `output_files` and are downloadable via `GET /output/{filename}`.

**So the backend does produce consolidated trial balance / BS / P&L / changes in equity / eliminations.** The question is the frontend.

## 6. Direct answer: does the frontend display actual consolidated statements, eliminations, issues, etc.?

**Readiness / summary / stages / entity status / issues / tool calls / AI reasoning: YES** — all rendered on `/dashboard/consolidation` from the real API response.

**Actual consolidated trial balance / balance sheet / P&L / changes in equity / eliminations / control figures: NO.** The backend produces and persists them, and the TS types declare them, but **no component reads them.** Evidence (grep for `control_figures|statements|consolidated_summary|output_files` in `frontend/src`):

- `types/consolidation.ts:168-171` — declared:
```ts
consolidated_summary: ConsolidatedSummary | null;
control_figures: ControlFigures | null;
statements: Statements | null;
output_files: OutputFile[];
```
- `types/consolidation.ts:227` — `/** The three group statements. */`
- No hits in `consolidation-dashboard.tsx` for any of these fields.
- `reports/page.tsx:20` still says *"This module **will** render the statements produced by the deterministic accounting engine..."* (future tense) and uses `PlaceholderPanel`.
- `runs/page.tsx:20` says the run history module *"will list consolidation runs..."* — even though `listConsolidationRuns()` exists unused.
- `issues/page.tsx` is placeholder even though the consolidation dashboard *does* render `run.issues` inline.

**Both the Reports page and the Issues page are placeholders**, and the only place issues appear is inside the consolidation dashboard card (§5, lines 725-745). The consolidated statements and the 7 output deliverables are **not surfaced in the UI at all** — they would only be reachable through the unused `GET /output/{filename}` endpoint.

### Notable gaps / inconsistencies
1. **Reports page unimplemented** despite backend fully producing `statements` (BS/P&L/changes-in-equity) and control figures — data is present in `ConsolidationRun.statements` but never rendered.
2. **Runs page unimplemented** despite `listConsolidationRuns()` being implemented in `lib/consolidation.ts` and the `GET /runs` endpoint returning headline figures.
3. **No eliminations view** — `eliminations.csv` is written and downloadable, but no UI and no type for it (it's not in `skill_data`; only reachable as a file).
4. **`Any` not imported** in `backend/app/api/consolidations.py:101` (benign at runtime because only used in an annotation body, but a type-check error).
5. **Skill docstring vs. implementation drift** — `consolidation.py:13-24` claims translation/elimination/statements are "blocked (no service exists yet)", but lines 302-341 and `STAGE_ORDER` (all `implemented=True`) show full assembly is wired and runs. The module-level claim is stale.
6. **`_jsonable` used for control_figures but `statements` is passed through raw** (line 137) — statements contain `Decimal`s, which FastAPI's `response_model` validates, but the stored `skill_data` (line 134) is `_jsonable`-converted while `statements` (line 137) is not; this is an asymmetry in the persisted record versus the response model.

1: """FX rate infrastructure (Stage 1).
2: 
3: Loads the recorded rates from ``fx_rates.csv`` (via the existing
4: :class:`SourceDataService`) and resolves a conversion between two currencies

7: Resolution order, all using **the same rate type** as requested:

9: 1. **Direct** — a recorded ``(base -> quote)`` rate for that type.
10: 2. **Inverse** — a recorded ``(quote -> base)`` rate of that type, used as
11:    ``1 / rate``. Justified because the source ``convention`` column states
12:    the rate as "X per 1 base", so the reciprocal is the exact same-type
13:    inverse quote (confirmed by policy review).
14: 3. **Cross** — no direct or inverse pair, but a single intermediate currency
15:    connects them: ``rate(base -> quote) = rate(base -> via) * rate(via -> quote)``
16:    where each leg is itself resolved direct-or-inverse. This implements the
17:    policy rule "use the product of the two given rates of the same type
18:    (for example, GBP/INR closing = GBP/USD closing x USD/INR closing)".
19: 
20: A **missing** rate is a typed :class:`MissingFXRateError` — never a number.
21: A recorded **zero** rate is a valid Decimal zero, distinguishable from
22: missing; inverting a zero rate is impossible and raises

24: 
25: No rate is ever invented: every returned Decimal is derived only from values

177:                 quote_currency=quote,
178:                 rate_type=rtype,
179:                 rate=_ONE / inverse.rate,
180:                 method="inverse",
181:                 legs=(inverse,),
182:             )
183: 
184:         # 3. Cross-rate via a shared intermediate currency.
185:         for via in self._cross_candidates(base, quote):
186:             first = self._try_convert(base, via, rtype)
187:             second = self._try_convert(via, quote, rtype)
188:             if first is not None and second is not None:
189:                 return ResolvedRate(

192:                     rate_type=rtype,
193:                     rate=first.rate * second.rate,
194:                     method="cross",
195:                     legs=first.legs + second.legs,
196:                     via=via,

199:         raise MissingFXRateError(

212:         """Currencies that appear on both ends of either requested currency."""
213:         connected: set[str] = set()
214:         for rate in self.rates:
215:             for currency in (rate.base_currency, rate.quote_currency):
216:                 if currency not in (base, quote):
217:                     connected.add(currency)
218:         return sorted(connected)
219: 
220:     def _try_convert(
221:         self, base: str, quote: str, rate_type: FXRateType
222:     ) -> ResolvedRate | None:
223:         """Direct-or-inverse resolution for one leg; ``None`` when absent."""
224:         if base == quote:
225:             return ResolvedRate(base, quote, rate_type, _ONE, "identity")
226:         direct = self._single(base, quote, rate_type)
227:         if direct is not None:
228:             return ResolvedRate(base, quote, rate_type, direct.rate, "direct", (direct,))
229:         inverse = self._single(quote, base, rate_type)
230:         if inverse is not None and inverse.rate != 0:
231:             return ResolvedRate(
232:                 base, quote, rate_type, _ONE / inverse.rate, "inverse", (inverse,)
233:             )
234:         return None
235: 
236:     # -- convenience -------------------------------------------------------
237: 
238:     def convert(
239:         self,

249:         """

278:             nci_share_of_profit_gbp=nci_share * resolved.rate,
279:         )
280: 
281: 
282: def entity_currency(entity: str) -> str:
283:     """Functional currency for a known entity id (from the entity master)."""
284:     return {"US": "USD", "UK": "GBP", "IN": "INR"}.get(entity.upper(), "GBP")

Used to verify\nthe engine's output (assignment: \"figures you recomputed independently\").\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport json\nfrom decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\nD = ROOT / \"data\" / \"northwind\"\n\nQ = Decimal(\"0.01\")\n\n\ndef r2(x: Decimal) -> Decimal:\n    return x.quantize(Q, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)\n\n\n# --- rates (GBP per unit of foreign currency) ------------------------------\n# fx_rates.csv: GBP/USD quote = USD per 1 GBP  =>  GBP per 1 USD = 1/quote.\nusd_closing = Decimal(\"1\") / Decimal(\"1.2530\")\nusd_average = Decimal(\"1\") / Decimal(\"1.2780\")\n# USD/INR quote = INR per 1 USD => INR per GBP = 1.2530*85.62 etc.\n# GBP per 1 INR = 1 / (GBP/USD * USD/INR) at matching type.\ninr_closing = Decimal(\"1\") / (Decimal(\"1.2530\") * Decimal(\"85.62\"))\ninr_h2 = Decimal(\"1\") / (Decimal(\"1.2840\") * Decimal(\"83.95\"))\nprint(\"rates: usd_closing\", usd_closing, \"inr_closing\", inr_closing)\nprint(\"rates: usd_avg\", usd_average, \"inr_h2\", inr_h2)\n\n# --- trial balances --------------------------------------------------------\nimport csv\n\n\ndef read_tb_us():\n    out = {}\n    for i, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader((D / \"tb_us.csv\").open())):\n        out[row[\"account_code\"]] = (Decimal(row[\"debit\"]), Decimal(row[\"credit\"]))\n    return out\n\n\ndef read_tb_uk():\n    # Valid = FY2024 dated and balanced.\nentries = json.load((D / \"adjustments.json\").open())[\"entries\"]\n\n\ndef classify_journals():\n    seen = {}\n    decisions = {}\n    for e in entries:\n        jid = e[\"id\"]\n        d = sum(Decimal(l.get(\"debit\", \"0\") or \"0\") for l in e[\"lines\"])\n        c = sum(Decimal(l.get(\"credit\", \"0\") or \"0\") for l in e[\"lines\"])\n        key = tuple(sorted((l[\"account\"], str(l.get(\"debit\")), str(l.get(\"credit\"))) for l in e[\"lines\"]))\n        if not e[\"date\"].startswith(\"2024\"):\n            decisions[jid] = \"excluded\"\n        elif d != c:\n            decisions[jid] = \"rejected\"\n        elif key in seen:\n            decisions[jid] = \"flagged\"\n        else:\n            seen[key] = jid\n            decisions[jid] = \"posted\"\n    return decisions\n\n\ndecisions = classify_journals()\nposted = {k for k, v in decisions.items() if v == \"posted\"}\nprint(\"\\njournal decisions:\", {k: decisions[k] for k in l[\"account\"]\n            if entity == \"US\":\n                g = acct\n            else:\n                g = mapping.get(acct)\n            if g is None:\n                print(\"  journal         cur[1] += Decimal(l.get(\"credit\", \"0\") or \"0\")\n    return {k: (v[0], v[1]) for k, v in out.items()}\n\n\nus_g = apply_journals(us_group(), {}, \"US\")\nuk_g = IC_EXP, FX_ACC = \"1250\", \"2150\", \"4200\", \"6300\", \"7300\"\n\n\ndef translate(group_bal, closing, income):\n    pl = {}\n    bs = {}\n    for code, (d, c) in group_bal.items():\n        if code 8: The eliminations are built from the deterministic reconciliation

11: 
12: * **Matched intercompany balance pairs** (group accounts 1250 receivable /

14:   the residual going to the FX account (7300).
15: * **Matched intercompany income/expense** (group 4200 income / 6300 expense)

17: * **Items in transit** are recognised by the receiving entity at the closing
18:   rate, then eliminated — no rate is invented, and the transit value is taken
19:   from the reconciliation's closing-rate conversion.
20: * **Unmatched intercompany** rows are never force-eliminated; they are
21:   reported for human review.

23: Every elimination line is a balanced journal (debits == credits) and carries

128:         """Produce elimination journals for one reconciliation."""

130:         review: list[str] = []

829:                     proposal={proposal}

858:                   </ul>

860:               </div>

862:           </CardContent>

887:                   </span>

890:                     {event.event}
891:                   </span>
892:                 </li>
893:               ))}
894:             </ol>
895:           </CardContent>
896:         </Card>
897:       ) : null}
898:     </div>
899:   );

Consolidated trial balance (GBP)\n        </CardTitle>\n        <CardDescription>\n          Every balance with the source rows that produced it. Debits equal\n          credits.\n        </CardDescription>\n      </CardHeader>\n      <CardContent className=\"overflow-x-auto\">\n        <table className=\"w-full text-sm\">\n          <thead>\n            <tr className=\"border-b border-slate-200 text-left text-xs tracking-wide text-slate-500 uppercase\">\n              <th className=\"py-2 pr-3 font-medium\">Code</th>\n              <th className=\"py-2 pr-3 font-medium\">Account</th>\n              <th className=\"py-2 pr-3 text-right font-medium\">Debit</th>\n              <th className=\"py-2 pr-3 text-right font-medium\">Credit</th>\n              <th className=\"py-2 pr-3 font-medium\">Sources</th>\n            </tr>\n          </thead>\n          <tbody>\n            {rows.map((row) => (\n              <tr\n                key={row.group_account_code}\n                className=\"border-b border-slate-100 last:border-0\"\n              >\n                <td className=\"py-1.5 pr-3 font-mono text-xs text-slate-500\">\n                  {row.group_account_code}\n                </td>\n                <td className=\"py-1.5 pr-3 text-slate-800\">\n                  {row.group_account_name}\n                </td>\n                <td className=\"py-1.5 pr-3 text-right font-mono text-slate-900\">\n                  {Number(row.gbp_debit) ? 11: Welcome to the Next.js documentation!
12: 
13: ## What is Next.js?
14: 
15: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications. You use React Components to build user interfaces, and Next.js for additional features and optimizations.
16: 
17: It also automatically configures lower-level tools like bundlers and compilers. You can instead focus on building your product and shipping quickly.
18: 
19: Whether you're an individual developer or part of a larger team, Next.js can help you build interactive, dynamic, and fast React applications.
20: 
21: ## How to use the docs
22: 
23: The docs are organized into 3 sections:
24: 
25: - [Getting Started](/docs/app/getting-started): Step-by-step tutorials to help you create a new application and learn the core Next.js features.
26: - [Guides](/docs/app/guides): Tutorials on specific use cases, choose what's relevant to you.
27: - [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference): Detailed technical reference for every feature.
28: 
29: Use the sidebar to navigate through the sections, or search (`Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K`) to quickly find a page.
30: 
31: ## App Router and Pages Router
32: 
33: Next.js has two different routers:
34: 
35: - **App Router**: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components.
36: - **Pages Router**: The original router, still supported and being improved.
37: 
38: At the top of the sidebar, you'll notice a dropdown menu that allows you to switch between the [App Router](/docs/app) and the [Pages Router](/docs/pages) docs.
39: 
40: ### React version handling
41: 
42: The App Router and Pages Router handle React versions differently:
43: 
44: - **App Router**: Uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries) built-in, which include all the stable React 19 changes, as well as newer features being validated in frameworks, prior to a new React release.
45: 
46: - **Pages Router**: Uses the React version installed in your project's `package.json`.
47: 
48: This approach ensures new React features work reliably in the App Router while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Pages Router applications.
49: 
50: ## Pre-requisite knowledge
51: 
52: Our documentation assumes some familiarity with web development. Before getting started, it'll help if you're comfortable with:
53: 
54: - HTML
55: - CSS
56: - JavaScript
57: - React
58: 
59: If you're new to React or need a refresher, we recommend starting with our [React Foundations course](/learn/react-foundations), and the [Next.js Foundations course](/learn/dashboard-app) that has you building an application as you learn.
60: 
61: ## Accessibility
62: 
63: For the best experience when using a screen reader, we recommend using Firefox and NVDA, or Safari and VoiceOver.
64: 
65: ## Join our Community

324:   ai_anomaly_investigation: "AI anomaly investigation",

330:   string,

333:   completed: {

335:     badge: "bg-violet-50 text-violet-700 ring-1 ring-violet-600/20",

346:     dot: "bg-rose-500",
347:   },

355: function aiStageLabel(stage: string): string {
356:   return AI_STAGE_LABELS[stage] ?? titleCase(stage);
357: }
358: 
359: /** Total latency and token usage across a stage's recorded LLM calls. */
360: function summarizeCalls(stage: AIStage): {
361:   calls: number;
362:   failed: number;
363:   latencyMs: number;
364:   tokens: number | null;
365: } {
366:   const calls = stage.call_records ?? [];
367:   const latencyMs = calls.reduce((sum, c) => sum + (c.latency_ms ?? 0), 0);
368:   const tokens = calls.reduce(
369:     (sum, c) => sum + (c.total_tokens ?? 0),
370:     calls.length > 0 ? 0 : 0,
371:   );
372:   return {
373:     calls: calls.length,
374:     failed: calls.filter((c) => !c.ok).length,
375:     latencyMs,
376:     tokens: tokens > 0 ? tokens : null,
377:   };
378: }
379: 
380: function AIStageRow({ stage }: { stage: AIStage }) {
381:   const meta = AI_STAGE_META[stage.status] ?? AI_STAGE_META.skipped;
382:   const summary = summarizeCalls(stage);
383:   return (
384:     <div className="flex items-start justify-between gap-4 py-2.5">
385:       <div className="flex min-w-0 items-start gap-3">
386:         <span className={cn("mt-1.5 size-2 shrink-0 rounded-full", meta.dot)} />
387:         <div className="min-w-0">
388:           <p className="text-sm font-medium text-slate-800">
389:             {aiStageLabel(stage.stage)}
390:           </p>
391:           {stage.detail ? (
392:             <p className="mt-0.5 text-xs leading-relaxed text-slate-500">
393:               {stage.detail}
394:             </p>
395:           ) : null}
396:           {summary.calls > 0 ? (
397:             <p className="mt-0.5 font-mono text-[11px] text-slate-400">
398:               {summary.calls} LLM call{summary.calls === 1 ? "" : "s"}
399:               {summary.failed > 0 ? ` · ${summary.failed} failed` : ""}
400:               {summary.latencyMs > 0
401:                 ? ` · ${formatDuration(summary.latencyMs)}`
402:                 : ""}
403:               {summary.tokens ? ` · ${summary.tokens} tokens` : ""}
404:             </p>
405:           ) : null}
406:         </div>
407:       </div>
408:       <span
409:         className={cn(
410:           "inline-flex shrink-0 rounded-4xl px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium",
411:           meta.badge,
412:         )}
413:       >
414:         {meta.label}
415:       </span>
416:     </div>
417:   );
418: }

516: export function ConsolidationDashboard() {
517:   const [run, setRun] = useState<ConsolidationRun | null>(null);
518:   const [trace, setTrace] = useState<ConsolidationTrace | null>(null);
519:   const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
520:   const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
521: 
522:   const loadTrace = useCallback(async (runId: string) => {
523:     try {
524:       setTrace(await getConsolidationTrace(runId));
525:     } catch {
526:       setTrace(null);
527:     }
528:   }, []);
529: 
530:   const runConsolidation = useCallback(async () => {
531:     setRunning(true);
532:     setError(null);
533:     setTrace(null);
534:     try {
535:       const started = await startConsolidationRun();
536:       setRun(started);
537:       await loadTrace(started.run_id);
538:       // Reflect the run id in the URL so a refresh reloads the same run.
539:       const url = new URL(window.location.href);
540:       url.searchParams.set("run", started.run_id);
541:       window.history.replaceState(null, "", url.toString());
542:     } catch (err) {
543:       if (err instanceof ConsolidationApiError) {
544:         setError(err.message);
545:         if (err.body) {
546:           setRun(err.body);
547:           await loadTrace(err.body.run_id);
548:         }
549:       } else {
550:         setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : "Consolidation failed");
551:       }
552:     } finally {
553:       setRunning(false);
554:     }
555:   }, [loadTrace]);
556: 
557:   // Refresh path: if the URL carries a run id, load the persisted run.
558:   useEffect(() => {
559:     const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
560:     const runId = params.get("run");
561:     if (!runId) return;
562:     let cancelled = false;
563:     (async () => {
564:       try {
565:         const loaded = await getConsolidationRun(runId);
566:         if (cancelled) return;
567:         setRun(loaded);
568:         await loadTrace(runId);
569:       } catch {
570:         if (!cancelled) setError(`Run ${runId} could not be loaded`);
571:       }
572:     })();
573:     return () => {
574:       cancelled = true;
575:     };
576:   }, [loadTrace]);
577: 
578:   const readiness = run?.readiness ?? null;
579:   const entityOrder = ["US", "UK", "IN"];
580:   const entityKeys = readiness
581:     ? [
582:         ...entityOrder.filter((k) => k in readiness.entities_detail),
583:         ...Object.keys(readiness.entities_detail).filter(
584:           (k) => !entityOrder.includes(k),
585:         ),
586:       ]
587:     : [];
588: 
589:   return (
590:     <div className="space-y-6">
591:       {/* A. Header */}
592:       <div className="flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-start sm:justify-between">
593:         <div className="flex items-start gap-3.5">
594:           <span className="mt-0.5 flex size-10 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-lg bg-[#0a1428] text-blue-400 ring-1 ring-slate-900/10">
595:             <BarChart3 className="size-5" aria-hidden />
596:           </span>
597:           <div>
598:             <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2.5">
599:               <h1 className="text-xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-slate-900">
600:                 Group Consolidation
601:               </h1>
602:               {run ? <RunStatusBadge status={run.status} /> : null}
603:             </div>
604:             <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500">
605:               Reporting period{" "}
606:               <span className="font-medium text-slate-700">
607:                 {readiness ? `FY${readiness.period}` : "FY2024"}
608:               </span>{" "}
609:               · Presentation currency{" "}
610:               <span className="font-medium text-slate-700">
611:                 {readiness?.functional_currency ?? "GBP"}
612:               </span>
613:             </p>
614:           </div>
615:         </div>
616:         <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
617:           <Button
618:             onClick={runConsolidation}
619:             disabled={running}
620:             aria-busy={running}
621:           >
622:             {running ? (
623:               <Loader2 className="size-4 animate-spin" aria-hidden />
624:             ) : (
625:               <PlayCircle className="size-4" aria-hidden />
626:             )}
627:             {running ? "Running consolidation…" : "Run Consolidation"}
628:           </Button>
629:         </div>
630:       </div>
631: 
632:       {error ? (
633:         <div
634:           role="alert"
635:           className="flex items-start gap-2 rounded-lg border border-rose-200 bg-rose-50 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-rose-700"
636:         >
637:           <AlertTriangle className="mt-0.5 size-4 shrink-0" aria-hidden />
638:           <span>{error}</span>
639:         </div>
640:       ) : null}
641: 
642:       {run ? (
643:         <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-x-6 gap-y-1 text-xs text-slate-500">
644:           <span>
645:             Run ID <code className="font-mono text-slate-700">{run.run_id}</code>
646:           </span>
647:           <span>
648:             Trace{" "}
649:             <code className="font-mono text-slate-700">{run.trace_id}</code>
650:           </span>
651:           <span>
652:             Started{" "}
653:             {run.created_at
654:               ? new Date(run.created_at).toLocaleString("en-GB")
655:               : "—"}
656:           </span>
657:         </div>
658:       ) : null}
659: 
660:       {/* B. Consolidated financial results (the actual figures) */}
661:       {run && run.consolidated_summary ? (
662:         <Card className="border-slate-300">
663:           <CardHeader>
664:             <CardTitle>Consolidated results (GBP)</CardTitle>
665:             <CardDescription>
666:               Headline figures for the group, produced by the deterministic
667:               accounting engine.
668:             </CardDescription>
669:           </CardHeader>
670:           <CardContent className="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
671:             {(
672:               [
673:                 ["Group revenue", run.consolidated_summary.group_revenue],
674:                 ["Group profit", run.consolidated_summary.group_profit],
675:                 ["Total assets", run.consolidated_summary.total_assets],
676:                 ["Total equity", run.consolidated_summary.total_equity],
677:               ] as const
678:             ).map(([label, value]) => (
679:               <div
680:                 key={label}
681:                 className="rounded-lg bg-[#0a1428] px-3 py-3 text-white"
682:               >
683:                 <p className="text-xs font-medium tracking-wide text-slate-300 uppercase">
684:                   {label}
685:                 </p>
686:                 <p className="mt-1 font-mono text-lg font-semibold">
687:                   {formatAmount(value)}
688:                 </p>
689:                 <p className="text-xs text-slate-400">
690:                   {run.consolidated_summary?.currency ?? "GBP"}
691:                 </p>
692:               </div>
693:             ))}
694:           </CardContent>
695:         </Card>
696:       ) : null}
697: 
698:       {run?.control_figures ? (
699:         <ControlFiguresPanel figures={run.control_figures} />
700:       ) : null}
701: 
702:       {run?.integrity_checks && run.integrity_checks.length > 0 ? (
703:         <IntegrityChecksPanel checks={run.integrity_checks} />
704:       ) : null}
705:

16: This page will walk you through how you can fetch data in [Server](#server-components) and [Client](#client-components) Components, and how to [stream](#streaming) components that depend on uncached data.
17: 
18: ## Fetching data
19: 
20: ### Server Components
21: 
22: You can fetch data in Server Components using any asynchronous I/O, such as:
23: 
24: 1. The [`fetch` API](#with-the-fetch-api)
25: 2. An [ORM or database](#with-an-orm-or-database)
26: 
27: #### With the `fetch` API
28: 
29: To fetch data with the `fetch` API, turn your component into an asynchronous function, and await the `fetch` call. For example:
30: 
31: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher
32: export default async function Page() {
33:   const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog')
34:   const posts = await data.json()
35:   return (
36:     <ul>
37:       {posts.map((post) => (
38:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
39:       ))}
40:     </ul>
41:   )
42: }
43: ```
44: 
45: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher
46: export default async function Page() {
47:   const data = await fetch('https://api.vercel.app/blog')
48:   const posts = await data.json()
49:   return (
50:     <ul>
51:       {posts.map((post) => (
52:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
53:       ))}
54:     </ul>
55:   )
56: }
57: ```
58: 
59: > **Good to know:**
60: >
61: > - Identical `fetch` requests in a React component tree are [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) by default, so you can fetch data in the component that needs it instead of drilling props.
62: > - `fetch` requests are not cached by default and will block the page from rendering until the request is complete. Use the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive to cache results, or wrap the fetching component in [`<Suspense>`](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#streaming-uncached-data) to stream fresh data at request time. See [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for details.
63: > - During development, you can log `fetch` calls for better visibility and debugging. See the [`logging` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/logging).
64: 
65: #### With an ORM or database
66: 
67: Since Server Components are rendered on the server, credentials and query logic will not be included in the client bundle so you can safely make database queries using an ORM or database client.
68: 
69: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher
70: import { db, posts } from '@/lib/db'
71: 
72: export default async function Page() {
73:   const allPosts = await db.select().from(posts)
74:   return (
75:     <ul>
76:       {allPosts.map((post) => (
77:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
78:       ))}
79:     </ul>
80:   )
81: }
82: ```
83: 
84: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher
85: import { db, posts } from '@/lib/db'
86: 
87: export default async function Page() {
88:   const allPosts = await db.select().from(posts)
89:   return (
90:     <ul>
91:       {allPosts.map((post) => (
92:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
93:       ))}
94:     </ul>
95:   )
96: }
97: ```
98: 
99: You should still ensure requests are properly authenticated and authorized. For best practices on securing server-side data access, see the [data security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security).
100: 
101: ### Streaming
102: 
103: When you fetch data in Server Components, the data is fetched and rendered on the server for each request. If you have any slow data requests, the whole route will be blocked from rendering until all the data is fetched.
104: 
105: To improve the initial load time and user experience, you can break the page into smaller _chunks_ and progressively send those chunks from the server to the client. This is called streaming. See the [Streaming guide](/docs/app/guides/streaming) for a deeper look at how streaming works, including the HTTP contract, infrastructure considerations, and performance trade-offs.
106: 
107: <Image
108:   alt="How Server Rendering with Streaming Works"
109:   srcLight="/docs/light/server-rendering-with-streaming.png"
110:   srcDark="/docs/dark/server-rendering-with-streaming.png"
111:   width="1600"
112:   height="785"
113: />
114: 
115: There are two ways you can use streaming in your application:
116: 
117: 1. Wrapping a page with a [`loading.js` file](#with-loadingjs)
118: 2. Wrapping a component with [`<Suspense>`](#with-suspense)
119: 
120: > **Good to know:** Bots and crawlers are served differently from browsers. Next.js waits for data fetching to finish and sends the fully rendered page instead of streaming it progressively. See [Bots and crawlers](/docs/app/guides/streaming#bots-and-crawlers).
121: 
122: #### With `loading.js`
123: 
124: You can create a `loading.js` file in the same folder as your page to stream the **entire page** while the data is being fetched. For example, to stream `app/blog/page.js`, add the file inside the `app/blog` folder.
125: 
126: <Image
127:   alt="Blog folder structure with loading.js file"
128:   srcLight="/docs/light/loading-file.png"
129:   srcDark="/docs/dark/loading-file.png"
130:   width="1600"
131:   height="525"
132: />
133: 
134: ```tsx filename="app/blog/loading.tsx" switcher
135: export default function Loading() {
136:   // Define the Loading UI here
137:   return <div>Loading...</div>
138: }
139: ```
140: 
141: ```jsx filename="app/blog/loading.js" switcher
142: export default function Loading() {
143:   // Define the Loading UI here
144:   return <div>Loading...</div>
145: }
146: ```
147: 
148: On navigation, the user will immediately see the layout and a [loading state](#creating-meaningful-loading-states) while the page is being rendered. The new content will then be automatically swapped in once rendering is complete.
149: 
150: <Image
151:   alt="Loading UI"
152:   srcLight="/docs/light/loading-ui.png"
153:   srcDark="/docs/dark/loading-ui.png"
154:   width="1600"
155:   height="691"
156: />
157: 
158: Behind the scenes, `loading.js` will be [nested inside `layout.js`](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), and will automatically wrap the `page.js` file and any children below in a `<Suspense>` boundary.
159: 
160: <Image
161:   alt="loading.js overview"
162:   srcLight="/docs/light/loading-overview.png"
163:   srcDark="/docs/dark/loading-overview.png"
164:   width="1600"
165:   height="768"
166: />
167: 
168: Because of this, a layout that accesses uncached or runtime data (e.g. `cookies()`, `headers()`, or uncached fetches) does not fall back to a same route segment `loading.js`. Instead, it blocks navigation until the layout finishes rendering. [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) prevents this by guiding you with a build-time error.
169: 
170: To fix this, wrap the uncached access in its own [`<Suspense>`](#with-suspense) boundary with a fallback, or move the data fetching into `page.js` where `loading.js` can cover it. See [`loading.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) for more details.
171: 
172: This is why, while `loading.js` works well for streaming route segments, using `<Suspense>` closer to the runtime or uncached data access is recommended.
173: 
174: #### With `<Suspense>`
175: 
176: `<Suspense>` allows you to be more granular about what parts of the page to stream. For example, you can immediately show any page content that falls outside of the `<Suspense>` boundary, and stream in the list of blog posts inside the boundary.
177: 
178: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher
179: import { Suspense } from 'react'
180: import BlogList from '@/components/BlogList'
181: import BlogListSkeleton from '@/components/BlogListSkeleton'
182: 
183: export default function BlogPage() {
184:   return (
185:     <div>
186:       {/* This content will be sent to the client immediately */}
187:       <header>
188:         <h1>Welcome to the Blog</h1>
189:         <p>Read the latest posts below.</p>
190:       </header>
191:       <main>
192:         {/* If there's any dynamic content inside this boundary, it will be streamed in */}
193:         <Suspense fallback={<BlogListSkeleton />}>
194:           <BlogList />
195:         </Suspense>
196:       </main>
197:     </div>
198:   )
199: }
200: ```
201: 
202: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher
203: import { Suspense } from 'react'
204: import BlogList from '@/components/BlogList'
205: import BlogListSkeleton from '@/components/BlogListSkeleton'
206: 
207: export default function BlogPage() {
208:   return (
209:     <div>
210:       {/* This content will be sent to the client immediately */}
211:       <header>
212:         <h1>Welcome to the Blog</h1>
213:         <p>Read the latest posts below.</p>
214:       </header>
215:       <main>
216:         {/* If there's any dynamic content inside this boundary, it will be streamed in */}
217:         <Suspense fallback={<BlogListSkeleton />}>
218:           <BlogList />
219:         </Suspense>
220:       </main>
221:     </div>
222:   )
223: }
224: ```
225: 
226: #### Creating meaningful loading states
227: 
228: An instant loading state is fallback UI that is shown immediately to the user after navigation. For the best user experience, we recommend designing loading states that are meaningful and help users understand the app is responding. For example, you can use skeletons and spinners, or a small but meaningful part of future screens such as a cover photo, title, etc.
229: 
230: In development, you can preview and inspect the loading state of your components using the [React Devtools](https://react.dev/learn/react-developer-tools).
231: 
232: ### Client Components
233: 
234: There are two ways to fetch data in Client Components, using:
235: 
236: 1. React's [`use` API](https://react.dev/reference/react/use)
237: 2. A community library like [SWR](https://swr.vercel.app/) or [React Query](https://tanstack.com/query/latest)
238: 
239: #### Streaming data with the `use` API
240: 
241: You can use React's [`use` API](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) to [stream](#streaming) data from the server to client. Start by fetching data in your Server component, and pass the promise to your Client Component as prop:
242: 
243: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher
244: import Posts from '@/app/ui/posts'
245: import { Suspense } from 'react'
246: 
247: export default function Page() {
248:   // Don't await the data fetching function
249:   const posts = getPosts()
250: 
251:   return (
252:     <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
253:       <Posts posts={posts} />
254:     </Suspense>
255:   )
256: }
257: ```
258: 
259: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher
260: import Posts from '@/app/ui/posts'
261: import { Suspense } from 'react'
262: 
263: export default function Page() {
264:   // Don't await the data fetching function
265:   const posts = getPosts()
266: 
267:   return (
268:     <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
269:       <Posts posts={posts} />
270:     </Suspense>
271:   )
272: }
273: ```
274: 
275: Then, in your Client Component, use the `use` API to read the promise:
276: 
277: ```tsx filename="app/ui/posts.tsx" switcher
278: 'use client'
279: import { use } from 'react'
280: 
281: export default function Posts({
282:   posts,
283: }: {
284:   posts: Promise<{ id: string; title: string }[]>
285: }) {
286:   const allPosts = use(posts)
287: 
288:   return (
289:     <ul>
290:       {allPosts.map((post) => (
291:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
292:       ))}
293:     </ul>
294:   )
295: }
296: ```
297: 
298: ```jsx filename="app/ui/posts.js" switcher
299: 'use client'
300: import { use } from 'react'
301: 
302: export default function Posts({ posts }) {
303:   const allPosts = use(posts)
304: 
305:   return (
306:     <ul>
307:       {allPosts.map((post) => (
308:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
309:       ))}
310:     </ul>
311:   )
312: }
313: ```
314: 
315: In the example above, the `<Posts>` component is wrapped in a [`<Suspense>` boundary](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense). This means the fallback will be shown while the promise is being resolved. Learn more about [streaming](#streaming).
316: 
317: You can resolve a promise on the server with `await` or in a Client Component with `use()`. React covers [when to resolve a Promise in a Server or Client Component](https://react.dev/reference/react/use#resolve-promise-in-server-or-client-component). To share one promise with many Client Components instead of passing it as a prop, provide it through context. See [Using React's `use` within a Context Provider](/docs/app/guides/single-page-applications#using-reacts-use-within-a-context-provider).
318: 
319: #### Community libraries
320: 
321: You can use a community library like [SWR](https://swr.vercel.app/) or [React Query](https://tanstack.com/query/latest) to fetch data in Client Components. These libraries have their own semantics for caching, streaming, and other features. For example, with SWR:
322: 
323: ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" switcher
324: 'use client'
325: import useSWR from 'swr'
326: 
327: const fetcher = (url) => fetch(url).then((r) => r.json())
328: 
329: export default function BlogPage() {
330:   const { data, error, isLoading } = useSWR(
331:     'https://api.vercel.app/blog',
332:     fetcher
333:   )
334: 
335:   if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>
336:   if (error) return <div>Error: {error.message}</div>
337: 
338:   return (
339:     <ul>
340:       {data.map((post: { id: string; title: string }) => (
341:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
342:       ))}
343:     </ul>
344:   )
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js" switcher
349: 'use client'
350: 
351: import useSWR from 'swr'
352: 
353: const fetcher = (url) => fetch(url).then((r) => r.json())
354: 
355: export default function BlogPage() {
356:   const { data, error, isLoading } = useSWR(
357:     'https://api.vercel.app/blog',
358:     fetcher
359:   )
360: 
361:   if (isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>
362:   if (error) return <div>Error: {error.message}</div>
363: 
364:   return (
365:     <ul>
366:       {data.map((post) => (
367:         <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>
368:       ))}
369:     </ul>
370:   )
371: }
372: ```
373: 
374: See [Client-side data fetching](/docs/app/guides/client-side-data-fetching) for direct browser fetching, providing initial data from a Server Component, and coordinating a library cache with the Next.js server and client caches.
375: 
376: ## Examples
377: 
378: ### Sequential data fetching
379: 
380: Sequential data fetching happens when one request depends on data from another.
381: 
382: For example, `<Playlists>` can only fetch data after `getArtist()` resolves because it needs the `artistID`:
383: 
384: ```tsx filename="app/artist/[username]/page.tsx" switcher
385: export default async function Page({
386:   params,
387: }: {
388:   params: Promise<{ username: string }>
389: }) {
390:   const { username } = await params
391:   // Get artist information
392:   const artist = await getArtist(username)
393: 
394:   return (
395:     <>
396:       <h1>{artist.name}</h1>
397:       {/* Show fallback UI while the Playlists component is loading */}
398:       <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
399:         {/* Pass the artist ID to the Playlists component */}
400:         <Playlists artistID={artist.id} />
401:       </Suspense>
402:     </>
403:   )
404: }
405: 
406: async function Playlists({ artistID }: { artistID: string }) {
407:   // Use the artist ID to fetch playlists
408:   const playlists = await getArtistPlaylists(artistID)
409: 
410:   return (
411:     <ul>
412:       {playlists.map((playlist) => (
413:         <li key={playlist.id}>{playlist.name}</li>
414:       ))}
415:     </ul>
416:   )
417: }
418: ```
419: 
420: ```jsx filename="app/artist/[username]/page.js" switcher
421: export default async function Page({ params }) {
422:   const { username } = await params
423:   // Get artist information
424:   const artist = await getArtist(username)
425: 
426:   return (
427:     <>
428:       <h1>{artist.name}</h1>
429:       {/* Show fallback UI while the Playlists component is loading */}
430:       <Suspense fallback={<div>Loading...</div>}>
431:         {/* Pass the artist ID to the Playlists component */}
432:         <Playlists artistID={artist.id} />
433:       </Suspense>
434:     </>
435:   )
436: }
437: 
438: async function Playlists({ artistID }) {
439:   // Use the artist ID to fetch playlists
440:   const playlists = await getArtistPlaylists(artistID)
441: 
442:   return (
443:     <ul>
444:       {playlists.map((playlist) => (
445:         <li key={playlist.id}>{playlist.name}</li>
446:       ))}
447:     </ul>
448:   )
449: }
450: ```
451: 
452: In this example, `<Suspense>` allows the playlists to stream in after the artist data loads. However, the page still waits for the artist data before displaying anything. To prevent this, you can wrap the entire page component in a `<Suspense>` boundary (for example, using a [`loading.js` file](#with-loadingjs)) to show a loading state immediately.
453: 
454: Ensure your data source can resolve the first request quickly, as it blocks everything else. If you can't optimize the request further, consider [caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) the result if the data changes infrequently.
455: 
456: ### Parallel data fetching
457: 
458: Parallel data fetching happens when data requests in a route are eagerly initiated and start at the same time.
459: 
460: By default, [layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages) are rendered in parallel. So each segment starts fetching data as soon as possible.
461: 
462: However, within _any_ component, multiple `async`/`await` requests can still be sequential if placed after the other. For example, `getAlbums` will be blocked until `getArtist` is resolved:
463: 
464: ```tsx filename="app/artist/[username]/page.tsx" switcher
465: import { getArtist, getAlbums } from '@/app/lib/data'
466: 
467: export default async function Page({ params }) {
468:   // These requests will be sequential
469:   const { username } = await params
470:   const artist = await getArtist(username)
471:   const albums = await getAlbums(username)
472:   return <div>{artist.name}</div>
473: }
474: ```
475: 
476: Start multiple requests by calling `fetch`, then await them with [`Promise.all`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/all). Requests begin as soon as `fetch` is called.
477: 
478: ```tsx filename="app/artist/[username]/page.tsx" highlight={3,8,24} switcher
479: import Albums from './albums'
480: 
481: async function getArtist(username: string) {
482:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/artist/${username}`)
483:   return res.json()
484: }
485: 
486: async function getAlbums(username: string) {
487:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/artist/${username}/albums`)
488:   return res.json()
489: }
490: 
491: export default async function Page({
492:   params,
493: }: {
494:   params: Promise<{ username: string }>
495: }) {
496:   const { username } = await params
497: 
498:   // Initiate requests
499:   const artistData = getArtist(username)
500:   const albumsData = getAlbums(username)
501: 
502:   const [artist, albums] = await Promise.all([artistData, albumsData])
503: 
504:   return (
505:     <>
506:       <h1>{artist.name}</h1>
507:       <Albums list={albums} />
508:     </>
509:   )
510: }
511: ```
512: 
513: ```jsx filename="app/artist/[username]/page.js" highlight={3,8,20} switcher
514: import Albums from './albums'
515: 
516: async function getArtist(username) {
517:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/artist/${username}`)
518:   return res.json()
519: }
520: 
521: async function getAlbums(username) {
522:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/artist/${username}/albums`)
523:   return res.json()
524: }
525: 
526: export default async function Page({ params }) {
527:   const { username } = await params
528: 
529:   // Initiate requests
530:   const artistData = getArtist(username)
531:   const albumsData = getAlbums(username)
532: 
533:   const [artist, albums] = await Promise.all([artistData, albumsData])
534: 
535:   return (
536:     <>
537:       <h1>{artist.name}</h1>
538:       <Albums list={albums} />
539:     </>
540:   )
541: }
542: ```
543: 
544: > **Good to know:** If one request fails when using `Promise.all`, the entire operation will fail. To handle this, you can use the [`Promise.allSettled`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Promise/allSettled) method instead.
545: 
546: ### Reusing data with `React.cache`
547: 
548: For data access that does not use `fetch`, such as an ORM or database query, wrap the function in [`React.cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache). Multiple components can then call the function within the same request while sharing one result:
549: 
550: ```ts filename="app/lib/user.ts" switcher
551: import { cache } from 'react'
552: import { db, eq, users } from '@/lib/db'
553: 
554: export const getUser = cache(async (id: string) => {
555:   return db.query.users.findFirst({
556:     where: eq(users.id, id),
557:   })
558: })
559: ```
560: 
561: ```js filename="app/lib/user.js" switcher
562: import { cache } from 'react'
563: import { db, eq, users } from '@/lib/db'
564: 
565: export const getUser = cache(async (id) => {
566:   return db.query.users.findFirst({
567:     where: eq(users.id, id),
568:   })
569: })
570: ```
571: 
572: Server Components can call `getUser()` directly:
573: 
574: ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" switcher
575: import { getUser } from '../lib/user'
576: 
577: export default async function DashboardPage() {
578:   const user = await getUser('1')
579: 
580:   if (!user) {
581:     return null
582:   }
583: 
584:   return <h1>Dashboard for {user.name}</h1>
585: }
586: ```
587: 
588: ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/page.js" switcher
589: import { getUser } from '../lib/user'
590: 
591: export default async function DashboardPage() {
592:   const user = await getUser('1')
593: 
594:   if (!user) {
595:     return null
596:   }
597: 
598:   return <h1>Dashboard for {user.name}</h1>
599: }
600: ```
601: 
602: Since `getUser` is wrapped with `React.cache`, calls with the same `id` within one request return the same memoized result.
603: 
604: > **Good to know:** [`React.cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache#caveats) is scoped to the current request only. Each request gets its own memoization scope with no sharing between requests.
605: 
606: ### Preloading data
607: 
608: When a component renders after other blocking work, its data request starts late even if the request inputs are already available. Preloading starts the request earlier so it can run in parallel with that work and avoid a request waterfall.
609: 
610: To preload data, call the data-fetching function without `await` before blocking work, then call the same function in the component that consumes the result.
611: 
612: The data-fetching function must deduplicate matching calls so the component can reuse the request started during preloading. Use one of the following approaches:
613: 
614: - For `fetch`, [identical requests are memoized automatically](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization).
615: - For an ORM or database, wrap the data-fetching function in [`React.cache`](#reusing-data-with-reactcache).
616: - With Cache Components, add [`'use cache'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) to the data-fetching function. If the function reads request APIs such as `cookies()` or `headers()`, use [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private).
617: 
618: In production, matching calls to a private Cache Function can reuse the same result within one request. This lets a component reuse a request started during preloading without storing the result in a server cache across requests.
619: 
620: Keep the preload function next to the component that consumes the data. This makes the dependency easier to find if you move or remove the component:
621: 
622: ```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/item.tsx" switcher
623: async function getItem(id: string) {
624:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/items/${id}`)
625:   return res.json()
626: }
627: 
628: export const preload = (id: string) => {
629:   void getItem(id)
630: }
631: 
632: export default async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
633:   const item = await getItem(id)
634:   return <div>{item.name}</div>
635: }
636: ```
637: 
638: ```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/item.js" switcher
639: async function getItem(id) {
640:   const res = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/items/${id}`)
641:   return res.json()
642: }
643: 
644: export const preload = (id) => {
645:   void getItem(id)
646: }
647: 
648: export default async function Item({ id }) {
649:   const item = await getItem(id)
650:   return <div>{item.name}</div>
651: }
652: ```
653: 
654: Call `preload()` before another blocking request to start loading the item earlier:
655: 
656: ```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
657: import Item, { preload } from './item'
658: import { checkIsAvailable } from '@/app/lib/data'
659: 
660: export default async function Page({
661:   params,
662: }: {
663:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
664: }) {
665:   const { id } = await params
666: 
667:   preload(id)
668:   const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable(id)
669: 
670:   return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
671: }
672: ```
673: 
674: ```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.js" switcher
675: import Item, { preload } from './item'
676: import { checkIsAvailable } from '@/app/lib/data'
677: 
678: export default async function Page({ params }) {
679:   const { id } = await params
680: 
681:   preload(id)
682:   const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable(id)
683: 
684:   return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
685: }
686: ```
687: 
688: The item request continues while `checkIsAvailable()` runs. If the page renders `<Item>`, the identical `fetch` call reuses the request that `preload()` started.
```

11: 
12: By default, layouts and pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components), which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use [Client Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) to layer in functionality.
13: 
14: This page explains how Server and Client Components work in Next.js and when to use them, with examples of how to compose them together in your application.
15: 
16: > **Good to know:** For an explanation of where each component type runs and how the boundary works, see [The Server and Client Boundary](/docs/app/guides/server-and-client-boundary).
17: 
18: ## When to use Server and Client Components?
19: 
20: The client and server environments have different capabilities. Server and Client Components allow you to run logic in each environment depending on your use case.
21: 
22: Use **Client Components** when you need:
23: 
24: - [State](https://react.dev/learn/managing-state) and [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events). E.g. `onClick`, `onChange`.
25: - [Lifecycle logic](https://react.dev/learn/lifecycle-of-reactive-effects). E.g. `useEffect`.
26: - Browser-only APIs. E.g. `localStorage`, `window`, `navigator.geolocation`, etc.
27: - [Custom hooks](https://react.dev/learn/reusing-logic-with-custom-hooks).
28: 
29: Use **Server Components** when you need:
30: 
31: - Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source.
32: - Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets without exposing them to the client.
33: - Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser.
34: - Improve the [First Contentful Paint (FCP)](https://web.dev/fcp/), and stream content progressively to the client.
35: 
36: For example, the `<Page>` component is a Server Component that fetches data about a post, and passes it as props to the `<LikeButton>` which handles client-side interactivity.
37: 
38: ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,17} switcher
39: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
40: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
41: 
42: export default async function Page({
43:   params,
44: }: {
45:   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
46: }) {
47:   const { id } = await params
48:   const post = await getPost(id)
49: 
50:   return (
51:     <div>
52:       <main>
53:         <h1>{post.title}</h1>
54:         {/* ... */}
55:         <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
56:       </main>
57:     </div>
58:   )
59: }
60: ```
61: 
62: ```jsx filename="app/[id]/page.js" highlight={1,13} switcher
63: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
64: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
65: 
66: export default async function Page({ params }) {
67:   const { id } = await params
68:   const post = await getPost(id)
69: 
70:   return (
71:     <div>
72:       <main>
73:         <h1>{post.title}</h1>
74:         {/* ... */}
75:         <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
76:       </main>
77:     </div>
78:   )

80: ```
81:

84:

86:

89: }

91:

101: 
102: ## How do Server and Client Components work in Next.js?
103: 
104: ### On the server
105: 
106: On the server, Next.js uses React's APIs to orchestrate rendering. The rendering work is split into chunks, by individual route segments ([layouts and pages](/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages)), including [parallel route slots](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) whether or not they are displayed:
107: 
108: - **Server Components** are rendered into a special data format called the React Server Component Payload (RSC Payload).
109: - **Client Components** and the RSC Payload are used to [prerender](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) HTML.
110: 
111: > **What is the React Server Component Payload (RSC)?**
112: >
113: > The RSC Payload is a compact, serialized representation of the rendered React Server Components tree. It's used by React on the client to update the browser's DOM. The RSC Payload contains:
114: >
115: > - The rendered result of Server Components
116: > - Placeholders for where Client Components should be rendered and references to their JavaScript files
117: > - Any props passed from a Server Component to a Client Component
118: 
119: ### On the client (first load)
120: 
121: Then, on the client:
122: 
123: 1. **HTML** is used to immediately show a fast non-interactive preview of the route to the user.
124: 2. **RSC Payload** is used to reconcile the Client and Server Component trees.
125: 3. **JavaScript** is used to hydrate Client Components and make the application interactive.
126: 
127: > **What is hydration?**
128: >
129: > Hydration is React's process for attaching [event handlers](https://react.dev/learn/responding-to-events) to the DOM, to make the static HTML interactive.
130: 
131: ### Subsequent Navigations
132: 
133: On subsequent navigations:
134: 
135: - The **RSC Payload** is prefetched and cached for instant navigation.
136: - **Client Components** are rendered entirely on the client, without the server-rendered HTML.
137: 
138: ## Examples
139: 
140: ### Using Client Components
141: 
142: You can create a Client Component by adding the [`"use client"`](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client) directive at the top of the file, above your imports.
143: 
144: ```tsx filename="app/ui/counter.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
145: 'use client'
146: 
147: import { useState } from 'react'
148: 
149: export default function Counter() {
150:   const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
151: 
152:   return (
153:     <div>
154:       <p>{count} likes</p>
155:       <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Click me</button>
156:     </div>
157:   )
158: }
159: ```
160: 
161: ```jsx filename="app/ui/counter.js" highlight={1} switcher
162: 'use client'
163: 
164: import { useState } from 'react'
165: 
166: export default function Counter() {
167:   const [count, setCount] = useState(0)
168: 
169:   return (
170:     <div>
171:       <p>{count} likes</p>
172:       <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Click me</button>
173:     </div>
174:   )
175: }
176: ```
177: 
178: `"use client"` is used to declare a **boundary** between the Server and Client module graphs (trees).
179: 
180: Once a file is marked with `"use client"`, **all of its imports and the components it directly renders are included in the client bundle**. This means you don’t need to add the directive to every component that is intended for the client.
181: 
182: This behavior applies to components that are part of the Client Component’s [module graph](/docs/app/glossary#module-graph), which includes the modules it imports and the components it renders directly. It does not apply to Server Components passed as children or other props. Those components are not imported into the Client Component’s module graph. They are rendered on the server and passed to the Client Component as rendered output.
183: 
184: See [Interleaving Server and Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components#interleaving-server-and-client-components) for how Server and Client Components can be combined.
185: 
186: ### Reducing JS bundle size
187: 
188: To reduce the size of your client JavaScript bundles, add `'use client'` at the top of the files that define your interactive components instead of marking large parts of your UI as Client Components.
189: 
190: For example, the `<Layout>` component contains mostly static elements like a logo and navigation links, but includes an interactive search bar. `<Search />` needs to be a Client Component, while the rest of the layout can stay a Server Component.
191: 
192: ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={12} switcher
193: // Client Component
194: import Search from './search'
195: // Server Component
196: import Logo from './logo'
197: 
198: // Layout is a Server Component by default
199: export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
200:   return (
201:     <>
202:       <nav>
203:         <Logo />
204:         <Search />
205:       </nav>
206:       <main>{children}</main>
207:     </>
208:   )
209: }
210: ```
211: 
212: ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={12} switcher
213: // Client Component
214: import Search from './search'
215: // Server Component
216: import Logo from './logo'
217: 
218: // Layout is a Server Component by default
219: export default function Layout({ children }) {
220:   return (
221:     <>
222:       <nav>
223:         <Logo />
224:         <Search />
225:       </nav>
226:       <main>{children}</main>
227:     </>
228:   )
229: }
230: ```
231: 
232: ```tsx filename="app/ui/search.tsx" highlight={1} switcher
233: 'use client'
234: 
235: export default function Search() {
236:   // ...
237: }
238: ```
239: 
240: ```jsx filename="app/ui/search.js" highlight={1} switcher
241: 'use client'
242: 
243: export default function Search() {
244:   // ...
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: ### Passing data from Server to Client Components
249: 
250: You can pass data from Server Components to Client Components using props.
251: 
252: ```tsx filename="app/[id]/page.tsx" highlight={1,12} switcher
253: import LikeButton from '@/app/ui/like-button'
254: import { getPost } from '@/lib/data'
255:

257:   params,
258: }: {

260: }) {

262:   const post = await getPost(id)
263: 
264:   return <LikeButton likes={post.likes} />
265: }
266: ```
